cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the weighing is already running.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Live one conviction you actually hold where someone can watch, unhurried, this week. When they ask why, answer once and then go quiet.
cells.core:
You can tell what's true from what's almost true, and you've learned to say the true part at a volume people can take in. That's the practice kept up. In the small room where you refine by repeating, it shows: you check yourself before you speak, then you say the thing. Not the whole truth fast — the right part of it slow, and no faster than it can land.

What this balance is free to feed next: someone learning from you while you do the thing, not after. Live one conviction you actually hold where another person can watch it, this week, without hurrying. Let them watch your hands work. When they ask why, answer once and then go quiet. What they carry out will be the doing more than the reason, and that's the better carrier.
cells.sheetLine: You say the true thing at a volume it can land at.
cells.verb: telling the truth so it can be heard, on purpose

cells.tense: Some future conversation has you bracing before it has spoken one word.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Give the conversation you keep rehearsing a small piece only, then put it down. The rest can wait.
cells.core:
Where the practice is kept, you are rehearsing lines nobody has asked for yet. The correction no one invited is already drafted, and the discriminating eye that usually serves you well has gone running past the room, deciding what needs saying before anyone has said what they feel. The small room makes it worse — you rehearse alone instead of practising in contact, and a rehearsal nobody attends corrects nothing.

Step it down to a piece. Give the conversation you keep going over a small piece only, then put it down. The rest can wait. You are feeding a fire one stick at a time, not deciding whether the whole winter stays warm. Small and repeated beats the one long run you keep failing to make happen.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door the room has already moved past.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask someone close how it's been lately. When they finish, wait there and don't reach for the useful sentence.
cells.core:
The eye still works — you catch what's off before anyone says it — but nothing gets said, and with nothing repeated the sharpness has thinned into a habit of standing a step back. People near you read the quiet as distance, and the reading is fair. What you notice isn't landing anywhere, so it stops counting as noticing and starts counting as watching.

Come at it from the side. Don't try to practise the practice; ask someone else what it's like to be inside it. Ask someone close how it's been lately. When they finish, wait there and don't reach for the useful sentence. Their feeling has room in it for you too, if the answer is allowed to land and you stay put for a moment after it.

cells.tense: You are writing in a room and telling yourself you're only passing through it.
cells.act: make a ritual of the shared thing
cells.ask: Take one ordinary thing you and someone already do together — a meal, a walk — and give it a fixed shape: same time, same first move. Keep the shape.
cells.core:
You've been keeping a practice without calling it one — the way you name what's true in a conversation, gently, when someone nearby can't find the words. People leave easier and credit the conversation. The discernment did the work and got filed under good talk. You hear your own line come back to you, better made, and you don't mention where it started, because mentioning it would feel like claiming it.

A ritual is the simpler version of this — not keeping truth for people, doing one thing alongside them. Take one ordinary thing you and someone already do together, a meal or a walk, and give it a fixed shape: the same time, the same first move. The shape carries it. Inside the shape whatever gets said is theirs as much as yours, and you stop being the one holding it up.
cells.sheetLine: You keep others on course, then credit the conversation.
cells.verb: telling the truth so it can be heard, on purpose
cells.place: the small lit room where a practice is kept by repetition

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is 'you quietly keep things in proportion' — the record says the capacity is truth-telling tempered with discernment, not the bearing of others' feelings. A reader could reasonably say 'I fix things by naming them, not by holding them level.' The ask still works if my read is wrong: it asks a person already fluent in calibration to spend a moment being taught rather than teaching, and if they are nothing like my read, they still get a small honest exchange and a fact about someone's felt experience. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the room holds because of what you do quietly' — cut it before the draft goes anywhere.
